topic: Memory Hierarchy and Caching Strategies: Storage Devices
explanation: The memory hierarchy is a structured organization of storage levels designed to mitigate the CPU-memory latency gap. Levels are tiered by speed, capacity, and cost, ranging from the fastest, smallest CPU registers and L1/L2/L3 caches to slower, larger main memory (DRAM) and secondary storage. Caching strategies exploit the principle of locality of reference (temporal and spatial) to proactively stage frequently required data from slower levels into faster cache lines. This staging ensures a high cache hit rate, minimizing average memory access time (AMAT) and maximizing overall system throughput by keeping the CPU supplied with low-latency data.
